items.title: With 117 Million People Forcibly Displaced, UN Refugee Chief Tells Security Council ‘When Peace Fails, People Move’
items.summary: “Displacement is rapidly outpacing solutions,” warned today the head of the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in his first Security Council address since his election to the post in December 2025, urging the 15-member organ to fulfil its “unique” responsibility for maintaining peace.

items.title: Closing the New War Front in Yemen
items.summary: The Houthis’ rapid advance on the western Yemeni coast has opened a new front in the Middle East war that began with February’s U.S.-Israeli attack on Iran. A truce in Yemen is an urgent priority, so that hostilities do not spiral, drawing in more countries.

items.title: Sudan’s farmers are ready to return – private investment could get them there

items.summary: In Nepal, the World Food Programme (WFP) is delivering food and relief supplies to flood-affected communities in the north by truck, helicopter and humanitarian cargo drones. It has provided 127 metric tons of food to more than 15,000 people and is now delivering cash assistance to approximately 38,000 people.

items.title: Pakistan’s Sharif warns any diversion of Indus waters will be ‘treated as an act of war’
items.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif told the UN General Assembly on Friday that any attempt by India to stop, impede or divert Pakistan’s share of the Indus River waters “will be treated as an act of war”.

items.title: Nepal PM urges climate justice after ‘Himalayan tsunami’ devastates country
items.summary: Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah brought a stark warning from the Himalayas to the UN General Assembly on Thursday, saying catastrophic floods that killed at least 1,400 people in his country laid bare the human cost of climate change, and the failure of the international system to protect those least responsible for it.

items.title: Canada urges stronger partnerships as global order faces ‘rupture’
items.summary: Canada’s Foreign Minister Anita Anand warned the UN General Assembly on Saturday that the international order has entered an era of profound disruption, calling for stronger multilateral cooperation and new partnerships as major powers increasingly turn away from global economic integration.

items.title: Countries far from conflict paying the price for wars not their own, India tells UN
items.summary: India’s External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar warned on Saturday that violent conflicts continue to undermine international peace and security, while countries far removed from the battlefield are being forced to pay a heavy price.

items.title: Saudi Arabia warns Gulf security inseparable from global stability amid regional tensions
items.summary: Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Minister warned on Saturday that escalating threats across the Middle East risked international peace, energy security and global trade, calling for stronger international cooperation to protect Gulf States and vital shipping routes.

items.title: Cuba warns against ‘law of the jungle’ as Foreign Minister denounces US pressure
items.summary: Cuba’s Foreign Minister warned the UN General Assembly on Saturday that escalating military and economic pressure in Latin America and the Caribbean was threatening international law, while accusing the United States of intensifying a decades-long campaign to isolate and weaken his country.

items.title: ‘Safeguard the postwar order,’ China tells UN General Assembly
items.summary: China's Vice President, Han Zheng, urged the world to defend the postwar international order on Saturday, telling the UN General Assembly that geopolitical conflicts, widening development gaps and mounting global challenges make multilateralism more urgent than ever.

items.title: The Takeaway: UN General Assembly debate Day 4
items.summary: From the Caribbean to the Pacific, leaders from small island States demanded climate justice, ocean protection and greater solidarity at the UN General Assembly on Friday. They warned that rising seas are already redrawing national boundaries, while the ripple effects of faraway wars are being felt on their shores. This edition of The Takeaway summarizes key points made during the fourth day of the annual high-level debate.

items.title: Tuvalu urges decisive global action as rising seas threaten its future
items.summary: Climate change remains the greatest existential threat to Tuvalu, Prime Minister Feleti Teo told the UN General Assembly on Friday, warning that the pace and scale of international action are still falling far short of what vulnerable island nations need.

items.title: ‘No one speaks on behalf of Lebanon’: PM Salam asserts State authority at UN
items.summary: Lebanon’s Prime Minister, Nawaf Salam, has stressed that decisions over war and peace, and control of weapons, must rest solely with the State and its constitutional institutions.

items.title: LIVE: Six years on from COVID-19, is the world ready for the next pandemic?
items.summary: COVID-19 killed millions, shattered health systems and brought the global economy to a virtual standstill. World leaders are meeting Friday to review the lessons learned and cement a new approach to prevention and preparation for the next pandemic. Hopes are high that a World Health Organization-led international agreement can move forward.
